extracted.intended_audience: general readers of juvenile/children's moral fiction
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a 19th-century juvenile fiction narrative recounting boys' adventures and embedding explicit moral/social guidance (club rules, language advice, and standards for charity and discipline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Club conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have no profanity, no lying, no vulgar language; and no boy must be permitted to neglect his school, or his duties at home, on account of the boat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captain Sedley frames the club as a society for both amusement and the promotion of moral welfare; these rules are to govern meetings and behavior, and are to be enforced as part of the club's constitution. The club-room will contain a library and be used for instruction as well as recreation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of club members
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be careful whom you invite to join the club. We do not want any bad boys--especially none of the Bunkers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should be chosen for character as well as skill; specific 'bad' youths (the Bunkers) are explicitly excluded, while named local boys (Tony, Fred and Sam Harper) are acceptable. The selection is left to the boys, but with the father's admonition to exclude ill-behaved peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club officers and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: You will want a clerk and a coxswain... You will choose him by vote, as well as the clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles are defined: the coxswain steers the boat and serves as the captain/chairman of meetings; the clerk keeps records. The boys should create a constitution (regulations) for the government of the club rather than have adults impose it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership size and boat roles
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have thirteen boys; twelve to row, and one to steer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical organisation: the club-boat design (long, narrow, twelve row-locks) implies this fixed membership structure for operation and for assigning duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and expression standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Such expressions do not add anything to the force of language... You said 'By gracious!' Such phrases are apt to induce profanity, and are no addition whatever to the force of your remark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inelegant, slangy, or exaggerated interjections ('ripper', 'By gracious!') because they do not strengthen speech and may develop into profanity; cultivating careful speech is part of moral improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No neglect of duties for pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: No boy must be permitted to neglect his school, or his duties at home, on account of the boat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recreational clubs should not displace educational or household responsibilities; parents and club rules should prevent such neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club as vehicle for moral improvement and instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: I intend that this club shall be a society for the promotion of your moral welfare, as well as a means of amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The club should combine healthy physical exercise (rowing) with opportunities for reading and instruction (a library in the club-room) and structured meetings during off-season (winter gatherings on the frozen lake).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obedience to parents as duty and source of reward
rubrics_metrics.description: Let this beautiful boat, then, convince you that obedience to your parents is your duty, and ought to be your pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parental authority and obedience are presented as proper and eventually rewarded (the surprise gift of the boat), contrasting momentary resentful feelings with lasting benefits from dutiful conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity vs hypocrisy in charitable acts
rubrics_metrics.description: If he gave away his money because he thought it was an act of charity that would look well, that would make Frank and his father think better of him, he is rightly served; and I am disposed to shut him up in this room with a good book to teach him better... On the other hand, if he had made up his mind to sacrifice his inclination at the call of charity, he would not have felt as he does now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral worth of a charitable act is judged by motive: giving to 'look well' is hypocrisy and deserves correction; giving as a true sacrifice of inclination is genuine and morally praiseworthy. Parental discipline may be applied to teach distinguishing motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firmness in dealing with disorderly youths
rubrics_metrics.description: No use to be easy with 'em. The better you use 'em the worse they sarve you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncle Ben's approach: detain or restrain ruffians temporarily (e.g., make them prisoners on the island until parents arrive), give stern lectures, and avoid leniency that encourages worse behavior; implied endorsement of firm corrective measures for habitually bad boys.
